sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: How does one very large value affect mean and median?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 35 yes, 16 no; row 2: 15 yes, 60 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 9x + 6, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional kilometre travelled causes an increase of exactly 9 litres of fuel.
Each additional kilometre travelled is associated with an increase of about 9 litres of fuel.
Each additional litres of fuel is associated with 9 more kilometre travelleds.
The predicted value is 9 litres of fuel when x is 0.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.

items.prompt: A data set records 8, 5, 14, 13, 6, 17, 34. Give the mean and the median.
A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 158 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 16 yes, 57 no; row 2: 57 yes, 44 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 7x + 25, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
